  ### Git Worktrees

  A Git worktree allows you to check out and work on multiple branches of the
  same repository simultaneously in separate directories on your filesystem.

  Traditionally, switching branches requires stashing uncommitted changes,
  making temporary "WIP" commits, or cloning the entire repository into a
  separate folder. Making separate clones wastes disk space and network
  bandwidth because it duplicates git history and object storage.

  Git worktrees solve this by letting linked working directories share a
  single underlying .git repository. Each worktree functions as an
  independent workspace attached to its own branch while sharing the same
  commit database, remotes, and reflog.

  #### Key Benefits

  • Seamless Context Switching: Switch to urgent hotfixes on main without
  interrupting, stashing, or context-switching unfinished work on your
  feature branch.
  • Parallel Workflows: Run long-running test suites, dev servers, or builds
  in one directory while continuing active development in another.
  • Resource Efficiency: Shares the existing .git directory, avoiding
  duplicate packfiles and multi-gigabyte clones.

  #### Essential Commands

  • Add a worktree: git worktree add ../hotfix-branch hotfix
  • List active worktrees: git worktree list
  • Remove a worktree: git worktree remove ../hotfix-branch
